passages.original: nam deficientibus iis nationibus quas Traianus subegerat, Mauri lacessebant, Sarmatae bellum inferebant, Britanni teneri sub Romana dicione non poterant, Aegyptus seditionibus urgebatur, Libya denique ac Palaestina rebelles animos efferebant. quare omnia trans Euphraten ac Tigrim reliquit exemplo, ut dicebat, Catonis, qui Macedones liberos pronuntiavit, quia tueri non poterant. Parthamasirin, quem Traianus Parthis regem fecerat, quod eum non magni ponderis apud Parthos videret, proximis gentibus dedit regem.
passages.english: For since the nations which Trajan had subdued were falling away, the Moors were making attacks, the Sarmatians were waging war, the Britons could not be kept under Roman rule, Egypt was pressed by uprisings, and finally Libya and Palestine were displaying rebellious spirits. Therefore he gave up everything beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris, following the example, as he used to say, of Cato, who declared the Macedonians free because they could not be protected. Parthamasiris, whom Trajan had made king for the Parthians, he gave as king to the neighbouring peoples, because he saw that he carried little weight among the Parthians.
passages.notes: Parthamasirin: the name is given as the manuscript tradition of the Historia Augusta has it. The king Trajan installed among the Parthians is usually identified as Parthamaspates, while Parthamasiris was a king of Armenia, so the name here may be a confusion in the text.
